title: U.S. Senate (special) · Ohio

context.text: This is a special election to fill the remainder of the U.S. Senate term won by J.D. Vance in 2022. Gov. Mike DeWine appointed Jon Husted to the seat on January 17, 2025 after Vance became vice president. The winner serves the rest of the term, through January 2029.
Sherrod Brown defeated Ron Kincaid in the Democratic primary on May 5, 2026, 89.4% to 10.6%. Jon Husted was unopposed in the Republican primary. Bill Redpath was unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

priorities.text: Campaigned on his record in state government, citing a 'conservative, balanced budget with the largest tax cut in Ohio history' as House speaker and economic development efforts as lieutenant governor.

positions.summary: Cosponsored S. 3752, the SAVE America Act, a bill to amend the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

record.text: Appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine to the U.S. Senate on January 17, 2025, to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance.
Serves on the Senate Special Committee on Aging, Committee on Environment and Public Works, Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
As Ohio House speaker (2005-2009), signed off on a state budget he describes as including 'the largest tax cut in Ohio history.'

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 89.4% to 10.6%

priorities.text: Campaign website states he 'led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed' and 'successfully fought to cap the cost of insulin and reduce the price of other prescription drugs for Ohio seniors.'
priorities.quote: led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed

priorities.text: Requiring data centers to pay the full cost of their utilities so Ohioans' bills do not go up.
priorities.quote: We’re fighting to require data centers to pay the full cost of their utilities so your bills don’t go up.

priorities.text: Banning stock trading by members of Congress and their spouses, and barring them from becoming lobbyists after leaving office.
priorities.quote: No one – NO ONE – who serves in Congress, or their spouse, should be able to trade stocks.

positions.summary: Called the Trump tariffs a tax on consumers and proposed rebating tariff costs to Ohio households.
positions.quote: Part of the reason for that is these tariffs which were a tax on darn near everything they buy

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site issue page (Our Fight) added for priorities; it does not take a side on the guide's issue statements, so no further positions or statements were added. No 2026 debate or questionnaire answers found.

candidates.name: Bill Redpath
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Libertarian primary unopposed

priorities.text: Supports reducing federal spending, warning of a possible debt crisis, and wants the Federal Reserve to focus solely on an inflation target rather than a 'dual mandate' that also targets employment.
Calls for repealing all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, in favor of 'unilateral free trade.'
priorities.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

priorities.text: Supports open immigration except for criminals, terrorists, and others who would pose a danger, and opposes U.S. military interventionism.

positions.summary: Wants to repeal all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, favoring unilateral free trade.
positions.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

positions.summary: Supports open immigration, opposing broad enforcement/deportation, with exceptions only for criminals, terrorists, and those who would harm others.
positions.quote: All immigration should be allowed except for a handful of people who fall into the categories of criminals, terrorists, the seriously ill, or others who would harm the life, liberty, and property of people here.

statements.quote: The "special relationship" with the government of Israel only leads the US into problems. We should treat Israel like any other allied nation.

candidates.name: Gregory Levy
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website text, questionnaire or direct issue statements could be loaded. News coverage (WSYX/CW Columbus, Spectrum News, AP) describes him as a socialist candidate but does not quote him on the guide's issues. Not upgraded.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for Husted and Brown are added separately by script. Husted's positions are drawn only from campaign messaging on his record and priorities rather than explicit statements matching the fixed issue list, so no `positions` entries were added for him; see `priorities` and `record` instead. Sherrod Brown's and Bill Redpath's own campaign/Candidate Connection material supplied clearer stance statements. Biography gaps: Gregory Levy's campaign website gives no birth year, education, or dates of military service; Sherrod Brown has no active official bio page, so his biography draws on Ballotpedia and Wikipedia.
